images.title: 60°, 120° and the hexagon
images.purpose: Recap in three small steps how equal arcs give 60°, two 60° angles give 120°, and the side stepped six times closes a hexagon.
images.composition: Three equal panels side by side, left to right, joined by two small grey arrows, each panel holding one finished construction with plenty of white space.
exact_structure: Left panel: a dark horizontal ray from A to the right; one grey (#6B7280) arc centred at A cutting the ray at B, and one grey (#6B7280) arc of the same radius centred at B meeting it at C; the segment AC in reddish purple (#CC79A7); a small angle arc at A labelled 60°.

Middle panel: a dark horizontal ray from its vertex to the right; one long grey (#6B7280) arc centred at the vertex with two small grey (#6B7280) cuts on it, giving two equal 60° angles side by side; the outer arm in reddish purple (#CC79A7); the full angle marked with the caption 60° + 60° = 120°.

Right panel: a grey (#6B7280) circle with exactly 6 small grey (#6B7280) arc cuts equally spaced round it, and the 6 points joined in order by reddish purple (#CC79A7) segments to make a regular hexagon; caption below: 6 equal steps.
Between the left and middle panels, and between the middle and right panels, one small grey (#6B7280) arrow pointing right (2 arrows in all).
Point labels A, B and C appear in the left panel only.
rejection: the hexagon with more or fewer than 6 sides or with sides of unequal length
the 120° angle drawn as a single 60° wedge or captioned anything other than 60° + 60° = 120°
a protractor or ruler markings drawn in any panel
images.takeaway: Equal arcs make an equilateral triangle for 60°, two 60° angles make 120°, and six equal steps round a circle close a regular hexagon.
images.description: Three small finished constructions in a row: a 60° angle from two equal grey arcs, a 120° angle made of two 60° angles, and a regular hexagon inside a circle with six arc cuts.
images.context: Shown beside the practice concept for constructing 60°, 120° and hexagons, as a compact recap before the student uses the tool.
images.teaching_notes: Read the panels left to right and ask how each construction reuses the one before it.

image_decisions.why: Three finished constructions side by side recap how 60°, 120° and the hexagon build on one another.
